anna: quick thread 1 1 compact Create Model form: do we show 'Required' on every label, use an asterisk, or try a compressed 'Req' badge that expands on hover/focus? lexi: my vote: visible text (tokenized) is best for a11y. but i like the idea of a compressed badge that expands on keyboard focus so we save horizontal space without hiding semantics. make sure the expanded label is in the programmatic name. jamal: compressed badge sounds neat. UX caveat: on mobile we won't have hover, so it must expand on focus or tap. also ensure translators can place the word before/after the label via tokenization. mike: implementation note: don't hide required state behind purely decorative elements. if we use a collapsed 'Req' badge, append an sr-only "required" to the label DOM so screen readers get it. e.g. ``. claire: about error surfaces: inline is fine for single-field, but for business rules that span fields (e.g., shards + replicas contradiction) we should show a persistent summary at the top of the step with links that focus the offending inputs. folks on support like a pinned summary because it's visible while scrolling. lexi: make that summary keyboard-focusable and use `aria-live=polite` or programmatic focus on creation. also include short descriptions in the list items for context so screen reader users don't need to hunt. anna: layout shifts have been flagged by front-end team. prefer reserving the helper line under inputs so errors toggle text/color instead of inserting DOM height. any objections? mike: no objections. CSS suggestion: `.field-helper { min-height: 1.125rem; }` and error copy should replace the helper text instead of adding nodes. jamal: destructive confirms: propose a "confirmation friction level" scale — low/medium/high — and map actions to it. e.g., delete draft = low (toast+undo), delete model version = medium (checkbox + CTA), purge org data = high (typed-confirm exact phrase). This gives us a defendable rubric. claire: i like the rubric. For 'high' friction typed-confirm we need mobile affordances: prefill the field with the phrase and let users tap to accept? maybe provide a copy button so they don't have to type full org slugs on phones. lexi: accessibility for typed-confirm: never rely on placeholder. show a real label, and on mismatch show an element with `role="alert"` so it's announced. Example snippet: ```html
Text doesn't match exactly
``` mike: for summary->field links use anchors that call focus and scrollIntoView. also set `aria-controls` or `aria-describedby` so screen readers can relate the summary item to the input. anna: decision proposal to ship in the next component patch: 1) support a compact 'Req' badge that expands on focus/tap and always include sr-only required in the label for a11y; 2) inline errors for single-field issues with reserved helper height; 3) pinned step summary for cross-field/policy errors with focusable anchors and polite live region; 4) adopt confirmation friction levels and reserve typed-confirm for "high" actions only; 5) include accessible typed-confirm example (visible label + role=alert) and mobile copy affordance in docs. jamal: sounds good. can frontend build a small playground showing the compact badge behavior, reserved helper, and the summary bar? will help PMs and translators. mike: i'll open a PR with the playground + code snippets and the CSS token for the badge expansion. will include tests for keyboard focus behavior and NVDA checks. design-bot: Created tracking issue: https://redwood.internals/issue/9120 "forms: compact-required-badge + summary + confirmation-friction" :white_check_mark: anna: thanks! i'll update the Figma components to include the compact badge variant and the friction-level chart. :thumbsup:
